title: Rigveda 5.13: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.13: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.13 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 331r-331v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.text: <sup>1</sup>WITH songs of praise we call on thee, we kindle thee with songs of praise, Agni, -with songs of praise, for help.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.13.2-6 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 1, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 331v
translation.original_text:
2a̱gneḥ stoma̍m manāmahe si̱dhram a̱dya di̍vi̱spṛśa̍ḥ | de̱vasya̍ draviṇa̱syava̍ḥ ||
3a̱gnir ju̍ṣata no̱ giro̱ hotā̱ yo mānu̍ṣe̱ṣv ā | sa ya̍kṣa̱d daivya̱ṁ jana̍m ||
4tvam a̍gne sa̱prathā̍ asi̱ juṣṭo̱ hotā̱ vare̍ṇyaḥ | tvayā̍ ya̱jñaṁ vi ta̍nvate ||
5tvām a̍gne vāja̱sāta̍ma̱ṁ viprā̍ vardhanti̱ suṣṭu̍tam | sa no̍ rāsva su̱vīrya̍m ||
6agne̍ ne̱mir a̱rām̐ i̍va de̱vām̐s tvam pa̍ri̱bhūr a̍si | ā rādha̍ś ci̱tram ṛ̍ñjase ||
translation.text:
2Eager for wealth, we meditate Agni's effectual praise to-day, Praise of the God who touches heaven.
3May Agni, Priest among mankind, take pleasure in our songs of praise, And worship the Celestial Folk.
4Thou, Agni, art spread widely forth, Priest dear and excellent; through thee Men make the sacrifice complete.
5Singers exalt thee, Agni, well lauded, best giver of our strength: So grant thou us heroic might.
6Thou Agni, as the felly rings the spokes, encompassest the Gods.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 331v (numbered 4v by the scribe) (OPenn image 332, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.13.2 ‹-draviṇasyavaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 332r (numbered 5r by the scribe), begins in RV 5.14.4 ‹-jyotiṣā tamaḥ avindat gāḥ›. Verses 5.13.2-6 end on this page; 5.13.2 begins on fol. 331r (numbered 4r by the scribe).
